transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen, Marcus Reed, Sofia Alvarez (Redwood) — Priya Nair, Luca Bianchi, Danielle Park, Omar (RosaTech)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on integration path, decision drivers are security posture and latency/cost on batch ingestion workloads.

00:00:05 - Ava Chen (Redwood): hey everybody, thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes. quick quick intro round?
00:00:12 - Priya Nair (RosaTech): hi im priya, cto at rosa tech. we run several customer-facing assistants, and we re evaluating inference vendors for the onramp.
00:00:20 - Luca Bianchi (RosaTech): luca here, platform eng, mostly responsible for gateway and service mesh.
00:00:24 - Danielle Park (RosaTech): danielle, security.
00:00:26 - Ava Chen (Redwood): great, and im ava — lead ae. marcus and sofia are our se team. marcus, quick overview?
00:00:34 - Marcus Reed (Redwood): yeah thanks, so at a high level redwood offers hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and a private vpc/onprem control plane. today we want to understand your ingress patterns, SDKs you use, and what tradeoffs you care about — latency, cost, and isolation.
00:00:48 - Omar (RosaTech): quick note, we use langchain and some homegrown orchestration, and also a small set of llamaindex pipelines. we do batching of user messages into bulk embeddings and few-shot prompts.
00:00:59 - Sofia Alvarez (Redwood): ok good, adapters are straightforward — we have first-class SDKs and examples for LangChain/LlamaIndex, also a gateway proxy pattern where you run a local sidecar that multiplexes to redwood endpoints.
00:01:12 - Luca: can you explain the proxy pattern? we currently run kong as our ingress, then envoy sidecars.
00:01:20 - Marcus: sure, two common approaches: 1) gateway-side integration where Kong/Envoy forwards to Redwood public endpoints with token auth and client certs, or 2) onramp sidecar deployed in your cluster which handles batching, retry, and prefix caching and calls the Redwood backend. the sidecar helps reduce per-token calls and gives you local observability hooks.
00:01:45 - Priya: sounds like sidecar gives us more control. our legal/security team is worried about sending raw customer PII to hosted endpoints. danielle is nodding.
00:01:54 - Danielle: yes, we have requirements: audit logs retained for 2 years, customer data residency restrictions in eu; we also want kms-backed encryption and our sso.
00:02:04 - Ava: understood. we support customer-managed KMS for Private, and for Dedicated we provide options to integrate with your KMS through network peering. hosted supports encrypted transit and at-rest with our managed keys but we can do BYOK for dedicated/private.
00:02:18 - Priya: what about observability? we need traces tied to request ids and token counts per request for billing reconciliation.
00:02:26 - Sofia: we expose per-request telemetry (latency, tokens in/out) via our console and can stream events to your kafka or s3. we also have tracing hooks via OpenTelemetry; you can include request-id headers and we surface spans.
00:02:39 - Luca: ok, how do you handle rate limits and quotas? if we push embedding jobs we need higher burst capacity but also hard caps per customer.
00:02:48 - Marcus: there are two layers: edge rate limits (per-token / per-route) and account quotas (monthly token budgets). For Dedicated you can set custom quota policies and burst pools. On hosted we recommend a gateway-side token bucket in front of API to shape spikes and use our per-route limits as second line.
00:03:04 - Omar: edge case — when we do 10k concurrent embedding jobs, will you queue or fail? we need predictable backpressure.
00:03:11 - Marcus: we do continuous batching at runtime and will queue up to configured capacity. if you need strict SLA, Dedicated with reserved capacity is the right fit; hosted has fallbacks and automatic throttling which may return 429s under sustained spikes.
00:03:26 - Priya: latency numbers? our P0 is sub-400ms on short prompt completions and embeddings under 200ms for vector generation ideally.
00:03:35 - Marcus: depends on model. for small open models and optimized kernels we can get ~80-200ms median for single-request completions on hosted regional endpoints; embeddings vary, often 40-150ms per request. Dedicated reduces variance and we can occupy a GPU pool to hit your SLOs. we can run a benchmark using your real prompt mix and provide a percentile report.
00:03:56 - Danielle: can we get logs for every request? legal will want to correlate inputs->outputs for audit. also, how long are kv caches kept?
00:04:05 - Sofia: audit logs are available in Private and Dedicated; hosted provides limited request logs with configurable retention. kv cache TTLs are configurable in our runtime; if you deploy a sidecar you can opt to keep local prefix caches for X minutes to reduce backend calls.
00:04:18 - Luca: on the SDK side — we use LangChain and LlamaIndex. do you have connector examples?
00:04:24 - Marcus: yes, we ship official SDKs in python and node with LangChain wrappers and an adapter for LlamaIndex. we also supply example notebooks showing streaming responses and function calling.
00:04:34 - Priya: streaming + function calling is critical. we use function call to populate form fields in our app. any throttling on streaming?
00:04:41 - Marcus: streaming is supported. throttles are per-connection token rate; high-throughput streaming could be protected by the sidecar or dedicated pool to avoid head-of-line blocking.
00:04:52 - Omar: can the sidecar do batching for embeddings and also dedup caches? we have repeated identical requests across tenants.
00:05:00 - Sofia: yes the sidecar can batch and do prefix/k-v caching; dedupe is supported with configurable cache keys. for multi-tenant you can namespace caches per-tenant.
00:05:10 - Priya: how hard is setup? timeline for POC? we want a quick pilot in 2 weeks ideally.
00:05:16 - Ava: for a hosted POC, you can be up in a day; se will help set up the LangChain adapter and a small sidecar. for Dedicated or Private it may take 4-8 weeks depending on contracts and networking.
00:05:27 - Luca: networking specifics — do you support private link or peering?
00:05:30 - Marcus: yes, we support AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Endpoint, VPC peering, and on-prem VPN for Private deployments. For Dedicated we typically set up VPC peering and peer-managed KMS if needed.
00:05:41 - Danielle: what about data egress controls and ability to disable training/retention?
00:05:45 - Sofia: we do not use customer data to train models; retention controls allow you to opt-out of any storage, and Private deploys give you full control. Hosted is configurable but has managed defaults.
00:05:56 - Priya: ok, procurement question — price model for Dedicated looks like committed monthly, right?
00:05:59 - Ava: yes committed capacity with tiers and burst credits. Hosted is pay-as-you-go per token + embeddings. We can provide a cost estimate per 1M tokens and embed units with your workload.
00:06:11 - Marcus: also note our Optimize tooling can suggest quantization/batching to lower unit costs without big quality loss. we ll include those recommendations in the POC report.
00:06:21 - Luca: observability again: do you provide an OTEL exporter or do we need to pull from console?
00:06:25 - Sofia: we provide an OpenTelemetry exporter and can also stream logs/events to your preferred sink (kafka, s3, datadog). you can attach request ids and we ll include token breakdowns per request.
00:06:36 - Omar: about rate limiting; we use a per-tenant quota model. can redwood enforce per-tenant limits at the gateway?
00:06:42 - Marcus: yes with a sidecar/gateway policy you can enforce per-tenant token budgets and rate limits. Dedicated adds the ability to configure tenant pools and hard caps at the infra level.
00:06:52 - Priya: if we need on-prem for EU-only data, what does that look like?
00:06:57 - Sofia: private onprem package installs a control plane in your environment; we ship an appliance/containerized platform. networking is fully customer-managed and KMS is your key. it s the highest-touch route but meets strict residency.
00:07:09 - Danielle: will your audit logs integrate with our SIEM (splunk)?
00:07:12 - Ava: yes we ve onboarded Splunk and Elastic; we ll add the mapping doc.
00:07:18 - Luca: can you show a quick diagram of how the sidecar and gateway interact? (shared screen)
00:07:23 - Marcus: sure — (describes). envoys call sidecar which batches and does caching, then sidecar forwards to redwood regional endpoint over mTLS. token bucket is applied at sidecar and at edge. fallback policy routes to a cheaper model variant if capacity constrained.
00:08:05 - Priya: fallback is important. want to avoid complete service outage.
00:08:09 - Marcus: agreed, we configure automatic fallback chains and can route by policy: latency-first, cost-first, or isolation-first.
00:08:17 - Omar: any gotchas with LangChain chaining? e g callback management and streaming?
00:08:22 - Sofia: we ve seen customers need to wire our streaming callbacks into the LangChain LLMChain for token-level streaming; we have an adapter that handles that but you may need to tweak the callbacks for your prompt template.
00:08:34 - Priya: action items — we need the security pack and a bench run.
00:08:38 - Ava: noted. marcus will run the bench with your prompt set.
00:08:42 - Luca: timeline for bench results?
00:08:44 - Marcus: aim for 7 days. we ll show p50/p90/p99 latency, token counts, and estimated monthly cost across hosted vs dedicated.
00:08:52 - Danielle: also want documentation for data deletion API and retention windows.
00:08:56 - Ava: we ll include that.
00:09:00 - (Conversation continues with more technical clarifications and a short demo link share)
00:37:15 - Marcus: demo note — SDK repo link: https://redwood.example.com/sdk/langchain-adapter (shared), sidecar helm chart: https://redwood.example.com/helm/sidecar (shared).
00:37:34 - Priya: thanks, i will share our token distribution spreadsheet, it includes embedding vs generation split.
00:37:40 - Luca: one more: what about quota spikes from bad clients? can you block an API key automatically?
00:37:46 - Marcus: yes we support automated key suspension rules and anomaly detection; anomalies can be forwarded to your ops channel.
00:37:54 - Danielle: monitoring retention — how long are traces kept?
00:37:58 - Sofia: default 30 days on hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private. for long-term we stream to your s3.
00:38:10 - Priya: ok lets recap and next steps.
00:38:14 - Ava: recap: 1) Redwood sends security pack + sidecar helm + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples (Ava). 2) RosaTech shares workloads, token spreadsheet, and ingress config (Luca/Priya). 3) SE to run latency/cost bench (Marcus). 4) follow up call after bench to review results and decide hosted POC vs Dedicated trial.
00:38:37 - Priya: that works. target follow-up 2028-10-12.
00:38:42 - Ava: perfect. thanks everyone.
00:38:45 - (call ends, some outro chatter, recording stops)
